message: `effect(io, unsafe)` on `comma` names 2 effects, and an `effect(...)` tag names one
label: one effect per `effect(...)` tag
notes: a list here was read as ONE effect spelled with the comma in it, which nothing declares - so the claim could never be satisfied, and AX3010 reported it missing from a body that performed it. `restrict(...)` takes a comma list; `effect(...)` does not
help: write one tag line per effect: `;@axiom:effect(io)` and `;@axiom:effect(unsafe)`

message: `comma` touches raw memory and its declaration does not say so
label: __load64
help: this fires where the unsafe operation is performed, not up the call chain. The tag alone makes the declaration a trusted encapsulation, whose callers inherit nothing; write `;@axiom:precondition(...)` beside it as well when its safety depends on what its caller passes. If the operation is not wanted here the fix is to stop performing it, not to stop saying so
